about: What each measured CONFIGURATION is, and the controls a run of it must show in the same invocation before a silence counts as MISSED (tools/verdicts.py). An arm NAME in a case.json is a label; a corpus maps each of its arm names to one configuration here (corpus.json `arm_configurations`), so two corpora whose `spatial` means different things cannot be added up as if it did not. A control's expectation is part of the configuration's identity: a use-after-free control that COMPLETES is what shows an arm does not revoke, just as one that faults shows it does.

replay-arena.summary: the memory-contexts replay study's level 0 (ports/postgres/memory-contexts, backing-allocator.c): every chunk is an offset inside one arena capability; nothing is revoked

replay-sublet.summary: the replay study with PostgreSQL's managers patched onto Sublet context pools: every chunk is its own capability, revoked when the manager takes it back
replay-sublet.mechanism: per-chunk bounds and revocation in the nested allocator

app-level0.summary: an application domain whose SDK heap is level0 (CAPSTONE_APPLICATION_HEAP=level0): malloc bounds each object to its request; free revokes nothing; a nested allocator's chunks are unbounded inside the block it took

app-level0-pg-nested-sublet.summary: app-level0 plus PostgreSQL's memory contexts on Sublet context pools (ports/postgres/app/build-domain.sh, PGSU_NESTED=sublet): palloc chunks bounded and revoked; plain malloc as in app-level0
app-level0-pg-nested-sublet.mechanism: per-object bounds in malloc; per-chunk bounds and revocation in palloc

cheribsd-default.summary: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation at the platform default: malloc bounds each object; a freed object is quarantined and revoked by a later sweep
cheribsd-default.mechanism: per-object bounds in malloc; revocation after quarantine

virtual-mallocng.summary: the virtual Capstone profile (capstone/runtime/virtual, exact-bounds QEMU): the application runs as a Linux process under capstone-vexec with musl mallocng compiled for Capstone and run locally; malloc bounds each object exactly and free retires its lifetime, so a stale capability to it faults; a nested allocator's chunks are unbounded inside the block it took. Not the physical Sublet heap: its own lifetime mechanism (runtime/virtual/mallocng.md)
virtual-mallocng.mechanism: per-object exact bounds and lifetime retirement in malloc

virtual-mallocng-pg-pools.summary: virtual-mallocng plus PostgreSQL's memory contexts on the Sublet context pools, built for the virtual profile (ports/common/application/build-virtual.sh postgres with PGSU_NESTED=sublet): palloc chunks bounded and retired per chunk
virtual-mallocng-pg-pools.mechanism: as virtual-mallocng; per-chunk bounds and revocation in palloc

virtual-mallocng-replay.summary: the memory-contexts replay built as a Capstone application (capstone-application toolchain, virtual SDK) and run as a process under capstone-vexec: PostgreSQL's aset/slab stock on virtual mallocng, which bounds and retires each block it hands the manager but not the chunks carved from it
virtual-mallocng-replay.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of malloc blocks; none per chunk

virtual-mallocng-replay-pools.summary: the same replay with PG_SUBLET: PostgreSQL's managers on the Sublet context pools, their arena lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability (__capstone_sublet_malloc_linear), so every chunk is its own capability, retired when the manager takes it back
virtual-mallocng-replay-pools.mechanism: as virtual-mallocng-replay; per-chunk bounds and revocation in the nested allocator

virtual-sqlite-memsys5.summary: SQLite 3.22.0 built for the virtual profile with memsys5 stock over one static array (ports/sqlite/repro322/build-virtual.py --memsys5): every SQLite allocation is an offset inside that arena, so the system allocator -- virtual mallocng -- sees one object and no frees

virtual-sqlite-memsys5-pools.summary: the same with memsys5 on its Sublet port (build-virtual.py --sublet, ports/sqlite/sublet/sublet-3220000-memsys5.patch): the pool is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability, carved into one capability per block, each retired on sqlite3_free
virtual-sqlite-memsys5-pools.mechanism: per-block bounds and revocation in memsys5

virtual-pymalloc.summary: CPython 3.13.7's obmalloc as the pymalloc replay (ports/cpython/pymalloc, capstone-application preset, virtual SDK) run as a process under capstone-vexec: pymalloc stock, its arena one aligned_alloc block from virtual mallocng, every pymalloc block an unbounded offset inside it
virtual-pymalloc.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of the arena only; none per pymalloc block

virtual-pymalloc-pools.summary: the same replay with PYMALLOC_SUBLET in mode 1: the lifetime adapter owns an arena the virtual heap lends as one linear capability (__capstone_sublet_malloc_linear, aligned by borrow-aligned-block.h), hands out one bounded capability per pymalloc block and retires it on free
virtual-pymalloc-pools.mechanism: per-block bounds and revocation in pymalloc

virtual-ffmpeg-carve.summary: FFmpeg's carved corpus on the virtual profile with its carve on Sublet (-DFFC_SUBLET_CARVE): the block is lent LINEAR by virtual mallocng (__capstone_sublet_malloc_linear) and split into one region per carve, each issued as a bounded alias; a re-carve revokes the old aliases
virtual-ffmpeg-carve.mechanism: per-region bounds and revocation in the carve port, over virtual mallocng

virtual-wmem-libc.summary: wireshark/wmem-repros on the virtual profile with wmem STOCK on virtual mallocng: the wmem port's hosted build (preset capstone-application, -DWM_LIBC_SYSTEM=ON -DWM_CHUNKS=OFF), so g_malloc/g_free are the virtual heap's malloc/free at the requested size -- the build the CheriBSD libc arm ran. A packet-pool block, an epan BLOCK block and a jumbo are each one object to the heap; the chunks wmem carves inside a block are not
virtual-wmem-libc.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every block wmem takes from the system; none per chunk

virtual-wmem-chunks.summary: the same corpus with the wmem port's Sublet region and chunk layers in the process (-DWM_SUBLET=ON -DWM_CHUNKS=ON, shared/driver-virtual.c): the payload is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability (__capstone_sublet_malloc_linear), every block a region inside it and every chunk of the block allocator a region of its own; run in mode 1, a packet-pool reset and a chunk free revoke
virtual-wmem-chunks.mechanism: per-chunk bounds and revocation in wmem, over a payload the virtual heap lends

virtual-memcached-stock.summary: memcached/allocator-repros on the virtual profile with slabs.c/cache.c STOCK on virtual mallocng: the allocators port's hosted build with the stock ledger (-DMCP_STOCK_MALLOC=ON, as the ASan arm), built by the corpus's shared/build-cases.sh capstone-application, so every slab page and every cache.c object is one virtual-mallocng object -- a chunk carries its page's bound, an object its own, and nothing is retired until a page or object is given back
virtual-memcached-stock.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every page and object the allocators take from the system; none per chunk, none on a free-list transition

virtual-memcached-ledger.summary: the same corpus on the port's shared ledger over the Sublet authority in the process (-DMCP_SUBLET=ON, shared/driver-virtual.c): the payload is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability (capstone_borrow_aligned_block), every chunk and object a lease bounded to itself, revoked when slabs.c or cache.c takes it back (mode 1); with the carve remedy (MC_CARVE_BOUNDS) for 06 and 07, as the physical column 3 reads sublet-carve for them
virtual-memcached-ledger.mechanism: per-chunk and per-object bounds and revocation in the allocators, over a payload the virtual heap lends; for 06 and 07 also the item's key/suffix carve

php-virtual-zend-rounded.summary: PHP 5.0.0's own Zend/zend_alloc.c, compiled byte-identical from the corpus tree, running as a Linux process on the virtual Capstone profile over musl mallocng (capstone/runtime/virtual/heap.c): one malloc per emalloc (ZEND_MM is undefined in this build, so ZEND_DO_MALLOC is plain malloc), and the hierarchical wrapper (ports/php/engine/libc/php_capstone_zend_hier.c, -DZEND_CAP_BOUNDS_REAL_SIZE) re-bounds each result to REAL_SIZE(n) = (n+7)&~7. That is stock PHP's rounding, so up to 7 bytes of slack past every object are reachable -- the mechanism that hides 8 of the 31 cases from ASAN on an unpatched allocator. The HONEST-GAP column of the spatial pair
php-virtual-zend-rounded.mechanism: per-object bounds at the ROUNDED size; mallocng retires a block's lifetime underneath, but PHP's AG(cache) absorbs most frees so inner lifetimes are coarser than per object

php-virtual-zend-exact.summary: the same image and the same byte-identical zend_alloc.c, with the hierarchical wrapper re-bounding each emalloc result to the CALLER's request instead of to REAL_SIZE(n). The two arms differ in that bound alone -- same TU list, same ext/standard, same trigger on stdin -- so a catch here is attributable to the bound and nothing else
php-virtual-zend-exact.mechanism: per-object bounds at the REQUESTED size, over a block mallocng bounds and retires underneath

php-virtual-seam-stock.summary: PHP 5.0.0's own Zend/zend_alloc.c, patched with eight guarded hunks so that each emalloc's block is split into a 48-byte header and a payload region (ports/php/zend-alloc/sublet, -DZEND_CAP_SUBLET), running as a Linux process on virtual Capstone. PHP_CAP_MODE=0: NOTHING is revoked -- no per-object retire, and a freed block's loan is deliberately LEAKED rather than returned, because returning it would have mallocng revoke the block and catch the defect for us. A freed block therefore stays readable exactly as it does on stock PHP, and AG(cache) is live and absorbing most frees. The honest-gap column: what ASAN sees
php-virtual-seam-stock.mechanism: none: a freed block stays readable, and the cache absorbs most frees anyway

php-virtual-seam-block.summary: the same single image, PHP_CAP_MODE=4: the loan is returned on a real free, so musl's mallocng revokes per BLOCK underneath (runtime/virtual/heap.c), but this layer performs no per-object retire. Catches a use-after-free on a block PHP actually handed back; MISSES one on a block AG(cache) absorbed, which is the mechanism hiding 23 of the 31 cases from ASAN. This column exists so that a catch on the object arm is attributable to the SEAM rather than to the allocator underneath it
php-virtual-seam-block.mechanism: per-block, in the level below: mallocng revokes a block when the block is freed

php-virtual-seam-object.summary: the same single image, PHP_CAP_MODE=6: the payload region is revoked at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-taken under a fresh node when AG(cache) hands the block to its next tenant -- so the previous tenant's capability stays dead even though the bytes are live again. The header is never revoked, so zend_alloc.c keeps its own control flow byte for byte: the cache park still writes p->cached and REMOVE_POINTER_FROM_LIST still walks neighbour headers, all live. Differs from php-virtual-seam-block in the per-object retire alone
php-virtual-seam-object.mechanism: per-object: sublet_give on the payload region at every efree, over a block the virtual heap lends

php-real-stock.summary: PHP 5.0.0 built as a capability application from the Makefile's own PHP_GLOBAL_OBJS plus PHP_CLI_OBJS -- 145 translation units including main/ (PHP's runtime host), main/streams/, sapi/cli, TSRM/, regex/, all 65 of ext/standard and 39 of Zend/, with no SAPI of ours and no stubbed libc. Zend/ and ext/ are byte-identical to the read-only corpus (the build tree is a symlink mirror); the only real files are a php_config.h with two configure answers corrected for musl and, here, the patched zend_alloc.c. ONE IMAGE serves every arm: zend_cap_mode() reads PHP_CAP_MODE from the environment. PHP_CAP_MODE=0: the block the virtual heap lends is never returned, so NOTHING is revoked -- not by the seam and not by mallocng underneath it. This is the honest-gap column: stock PHP lifetimes, and the only arm in which a use-after-free is expected to go unseen. It exists because without it a catch cannot be attributed to revocation at all
php-real-stock.mechanism: no revocation anywhere; the loan is deliberately leaked

php-real-block.summary: PHP 5.0.0 built as a capability application from the Makefile's own PHP_GLOBAL_OBJS plus PHP_CLI_OBJS -- 145 translation units including main/ (PHP's runtime host), main/streams/, sapi/cli, TSRM/, regex/, all 65 of ext/standard and 39 of Zend/, with no SAPI of ours and no stubbed libc. Zend/ and ext/ are byte-identical to the read-only corpus (the build tree is a symlink mirror); the only real files are a php_config.h with two configure answers corrected for musl and, here, the patched zend_alloc.c. ONE IMAGE serves every arm: zend_cap_mode() reads PHP_CAP_MODE from the environment. PHP_CAP_MODE=4: the loan is returned, so mallocng revokes PER BLOCK on free -- but PHP's AG(cache) parks most freed blocks and returns without calling free() at all (11 buckets x 256 entries, index REAL_SIZE(size)>>3), so an efree the cache absorbs reaches no allocator that could revoke it. Differs from php-real-object in the per-object retire alone, which is what makes a catch here attributable to the PLATFORM rather than to the seam
php-real-block.mechanism: per block: __capstone_sublet_free_linear returns the loan, mallocng revokes

php-real-object.summary: PHP 5.0.0 built as a capability application from the Makefile's own PHP_GLOBAL_OBJS plus PHP_CLI_OBJS -- 145 translation units including main/ (PHP's runtime host), main/streams/, sapi/cli, TSRM/, regex/, all 65 of ext/standard and 39 of Zend/, with no SAPI of ours and no stubbed libc. Zend/ and ext/ are byte-identical to the read-only corpus (the build tree is a symlink mirror); the only real files are a php_config.h with two configure answers corrected for musl and, here, the patched zend_alloc.c. ONE IMAGE serves every arm: zend_cap_mode() reads PHP_CAP_MODE from the environment. PHP_CAP_MODE=6: the payload region is revoked at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-taken under a fresh node when AG(cache) hands the block to its next tenant. The header is never revoked, so zend_alloc.c keeps its own control flow byte for byte -- the cache park still writes p->cached and REMOVE_POINTER_FROM_LIST still walks neighbour headers, all live. The bound is PHP's own REAL_SIZE rounding, which makes this the CONTROL of the spatial pair as well as the fault arm of the temporal triple INSTRUMENT CONTROL: seam-bound-probe is probes/probe-seam stage 7, built from the same zend-cap-blocks.c and zend-cap-backing.c as this image. It emalloc's 9 bytes, reads index 9 under PHP's REAL_SIZE rounding (which must SUCCEED, proving the slack is reachable exactly as in stock PHP), then re-bounds exactly and reads index 9 again (which must FAULT). It therefore ends in a fault BY DESIGN and is declared identically on both spatial arms: it establishes that the seam's bound logic distinguishes the two arms, NOT that this particular image is running a particular arm. What establishes the arm is the ZEND_CAP_MODE line the image itself prints, which the runner gates on.
php-real-object.mechanism: per object: sublet_give on the payload region at every efree, over a lent block

php-real-exact.summary: PHP 5.0.0 built as a capability application from the Makefile's own PHP_GLOBAL_OBJS plus PHP_CLI_OBJS -- 145 translation units including main/ (PHP's runtime host), main/streams/, sapi/cli, TSRM/, regex/, all 65 of ext/standard and 39 of Zend/, with no SAPI of ours and no stubbed libc. Zend/ and ext/ are byte-identical to the read-only corpus (the build tree is a symlink mirror); the only real files are a php_config.h with two configure answers corrected for musl and, here, the patched zend_alloc.c. ONE IMAGE serves every arm: zend_cap_mode() reads PHP_CAP_MODE from the environment. PHP_CAP_MODE=7: as php-real-object, plus every capability handed to PHP bounded to the CALLER's request rather than to REAL_SIZE(size) = (size+7)&~7. The rounding is one of the corpus's two masking mechanisms and gives up to 7 bytes of slack, so this is the fault arm of the spatial pair and php-real-object is its control. Revocation is ON in both, so the control also exercises the machinery revocation-sanity exists to validate INSTRUMENT CONTROL: seam-bound-probe is probes/probe-seam stage 7, built from the same zend-cap-blocks.c and zend-cap-backing.c as this image. It emalloc's 9 bytes, reads index 9 under PHP's REAL_SIZE rounding (which must SUCCEED, proving the slack is reachable exactly as in stock PHP), then re-bounds exactly and reads index 9 again (which must FAULT). It therefore ends in a fault BY DESIGN and is declared identically on both spatial arms: it establishes that the seam's bound logic distinguishes the two arms, NOT that this particular image is running a particular arm. What establishes the arm is the ZEND_CAP_MODE line the image itself prints, which the runner gates on.
php-real-exact.mechanism: per object bounds at the caller's size, plus the per-efree retire
